answer: Each sail cloth is stamped at the sail loft and entered in the miller's book with the length of canvas and the date it was cut. A basalt sail sewn from unmarked canvas fails the mark: at the pigment of the cloth the weave must match the bolt the stamp names, and unmarked canvas has no story. Faking the stamp means buying a bolt of sailcloth, bribing a loft master and paying 5,900, while the mirror entry in the miller's book is read at every market, so a sail whose cloth was never stamped is turned away.
